events.title: Coffee With Someone New
events.text: {person:stranger} from the bookshop finally asked me out. We are meeting for coffee this afternoon.

choices.label: Go and be myself
choices.outcome_text: I went, I laughed too loudly at my own joke, and they laughed too. I count that as a win.

choices.label: Cancel at the last minute
choices.outcome_text: I texted an excuse and put the phone face down. The quiet felt heavier than I expected.

events.title: Washed Out
events.text: My first date with {person:crush} is tonight, and the sky has opened up like it is personally offended.

choices.label: Dance in the rain anyway
choices.outcome_text: We got drenched and silly, and the date was better than anything I had planned.

choices.label: Reschedule for next week
choices.outcome_text: We moved it to next week. They seemed relieved, and so was I.

events.title: The Long Way Round
events.text: {person:crush} suggested we just walk and talk, no plan, no restaurant, no escape route.

choices.label: Take the long way
choices.outcome_text: We walked until the streetlights came on. I did not notice the time at all.

choices.label: Suggest a café instead
choices.outcome_text: We settled into a corner booth and talked over coffee until it went cold.

events.title: Nerves
events.text: I am ten minutes early for my date with {person:stranger} and my hands will not sit still.

choices.label: Breathe and wait
choices.outcome_text: I breathed, they arrived, and the nerves turned into something warmer.

choices.label: Leave before they get here
choices.outcome_text: I walked away fast and pretended I had never been there. My heart took an hour to slow down.

events.title: Second Thoughts
events.text: {person:crush} is sweet, but my stomach says something is off. I cannot tell if it is instinct or fear.

choices.label: Trust my gut and step back
choices.outcome_text: I politely pulled away from the almost-kiss and said goodnight. Something in me unclenched the same evening.

choices.label: Give it one more chance
choices.outcome_text: I gave our relationship one more evening. I am still not sure if it was patience or stubbornness.

events.title: The Spark
events.text: {person:lover} reached for the same mug as me and neither of us moved away.

choices.label: Lean into the moment
choices.outcome_text: The air between us crackled like the first week all over again.

choices.label: Make a joke of it
choices.outcome_text: I joked, they chased me with a dishcloth, and the kitchen rang with laughing.

events.title: Slow Burn
events.text: Nothing dramatic happened today. {person:lover} just read beside me while it rained, and it felt like enough.

choices.label: Savour the quiet
choices.outcome_text: I put my feet on their lap and read the same paragraph four times, happy.

choices.label: Put the kettle on
choices.outcome_text: Two teas, one blanket, zero complaints.

events.title: One More Dance
events.text: At a friend's party, {person:lover} pulled me up for one more dance than I planned.

choices.label: Dance badly, happily
choices.outcome_text: I have never been a good dancer. Neither have they. It was perfect.

choices.label: Cheer them on from the side
choices.outcome_text: I watched them laugh under the lights and felt embarrassingly fond.

events.title: A Bold Compliment
events.text: A stranger across the room is smiling at me like we share a secret. {person:stranger} has confidence I envy.

choices.label: Smile back
choices.outcome_text: I smiled back, and the whole evening tilted a few degrees brighter.

choices.label: Look away politely
choices.outcome_text: I studied my drink very hard for the rest of our first date.

events.title: Aisle Five
events.text: {person:crush} and I keep reaching for the same shelf at the market. It stopped being an accident two aisles ago.

choices.label: Say something silly
choices.outcome_text: I commented on the tragic state of the tomatoes. They laughed. Progress.

choices.label: Keep shopping
choices.outcome_text: I let the chance to ask them out pass, and wondered about it all the way home.

events.title: A Kind No
events.text: I asked {person:stranger} if they would like to get dinner sometime, and I watched them search for a gentle way to decline.

choices.label: Accept it with grace
choices.outcome_text: When they turned me down, I said I understood and meant it. A kind no still stings, but it heals clean.

choices.label: Push a little harder
choices.outcome_text: I pushed them for an answer, and watched their patience close like a shop shutter. I deserved that.

events.title: Wrong Read
events.text: I was sure {person:crush} had been flirting with me for weeks. Today I found out they are happily taken.

choices.label: Laugh at myself
choices.outcome_text: I laughed at my own dramatic reading of the situation. Mostly laughed.

choices.label: Sulk about it
choices.outcome_text: I sulked for two days. My mirror suggested I get over it.

events.title: A Flicker of Guilt
events.text: Someone attractive flirted with me at the market and, for a second, I forgot I came here with {person:partner}.

choices.label: Find my partner immediately
choices.outcome_text: I found my person across the market and squeezed their hand. The flicker stayed a flicker.

choices.label: Enjoy the attention a little too long
choices.outcome_text: I let the flirty moment run a beat too long. Nothing happened, but I did not love how it felt after.

events.title: An Old Number
events.text: My phone lit up with a name I deleted but never forgot. {person:ex} wants to know how I have been.

choices.label: Reply, keep it light
choices.outcome_text: We traded a few careful messages. Some doors are better left as doors.

choices.label: Leave it unread
choices.outcome_text: I left their message unread and went to make tea with shaking hands.

events.title: Familiar Territory
events.text: {person:ex} suggested we get dinner and catch up properly. Old habits are offering me a chair.

choices.label: Go to dinner
choices.outcome_text: Dinner was easy in all the old dangerous ways. I am still deciding how I feel about that.

choices.label: Decline kindly
choices.outcome_text: I declined with real kindness. Growth is rarely dramatic.

events.title: The Conversation We Owed
events.text: {person:ex} wants to meet and finally talk about how it ended. Every version of this talk lives in my head.

choices.label: Meet and say the true things
choices.outcome_text: We said the true things. Whatever we are now, it is finally honest.

choices.label: I am not ready
choices.outcome_text: I said not yet. Maybe someday, maybe never. I can live with either.

events.title: They Noticed
events.text: {person:partner} saw the messages from {person:ex} on my screen before I did.

choices.label: Show the messages, reassure them
choices.outcome_text: I handed over the phone and answered every question. Trust is built in moments like this.

choices.label: Get defensive
choices.outcome_text: I got defensive about nothing, which made it look like something. Smooth.

events.title: The Bill Again
events.text: {person:partner} and I are staring at another bill that is bigger than either of us admitted it would be.

choices.label: Sit down and plan together
choices.outcome_text: We spread the bills on the table and made a plan. It felt like us against the problem.

choices.label: Point out whose fault it is
choices.outcome_text: I won the argument about fault and lost the evening entirely.

events.title: The Surprise Splurge
events.text: {person:partner} came home glowing about a purchase we definitely did not budget for.

choices.label: Ask about it calmly
choices.outcome_text: I asked before I judged. It turned out there was a story, and a receipt, and a plan.

choices.label: Let them have it
choices.outcome_text: I said the money was the point, but my volume said the money was not the point.

choices.label: Retail-therapy right back
choices.outcome_text: I bought something ridiculous too. Petty? Yes. Satisfying? Briefly.

events.title: The Hidden Statement
events.text: I found a statement {person:partner} had tucked away. There is a debt I never knew about.

choices.label: Ask for the whole truth
choices.outcome_text: The hidden debt came from shame, not malice. Ugly to find, easier to carry together.

choices.label: Go cold and quiet
choices.outcome_text: I went quiet for days. The silence cost more than the debt.

events.title: Small Wins
events.text: {person:partner} proposed we both take packed lunches for a month and put the savings toward something fun.

choices.label: Game on
choices.outcome_text: We became insufferable lunch accountants and saved a small fortune.

choices.label: I like my café lunches
choices.outcome_text: I opted out. They did it anyway and showed me the jar. I felt judged by a jar.

events.title: Dinner With The In-Laws
events.text: {person:partner}'s family invited us to dinner, and their mother has already asked me three questions I cannot answer correctly.

choices.label: Turn on the charm
choices.outcome_text: I smiled through the interrogation and passed the gravy. Diplomacy survives another year.

choices.label: Kick my partner under the table
choices.outcome_text: They caught my eye, took the conversational wheel, and rescued me mid-sentence.

events.title: The Backhanded Compliment
events.text: {person:partner}'s parent told me I look 'so much healthier than last time'. {person:partner} squeezed my hand too late.

choices.label: Let it slide off
choices.outcome_text: I let the in-laws' jab slide off me like rain off a roof. Their family, their weather.

choices.label: Vent the whole car ride home
choices.outcome_text: I replayed the comment with commentary for forty minutes. My partner took it like a saint.

events.title: Whose Holiday Is It?
events.text: Both families want us for the holiday. {person:partner} is watching me decide, and I can feel the trap loading.

choices.label: Propose splitting the day
choices.outcome_text: We did both houses, ate twice, and slept for ten hours. Worth it.

choices.label: Declare a holiday for just us
choices.outcome_text: We stayed home in our pajamas and let the phone ring. Glorious treason.

choices.label: Call both families instead
choices.outcome_text: We called each family and sang badly over the phone. It was enough.

events.title: The First Word
events.text: {person:partner} and I have not spoken properly in two days. The argument is old; the silence is older.

choices.label: Say the first sorry
choices.outcome_text: I said sorry first. It cost me nothing and gave back everything.

choices.label: Wait for them to break first
choices.outcome_text: I waited. The silence got comfortable, which frightened me more than the argument.

events.title: A Small White Flag
events.text: Things with {person:partner} are still frosty. Maybe a gesture would melt what words cannot.

choices.label: Bring home flowers
choices.outcome_text: Flowers, an eyebrow raised, then the smallest smile. Truce declared.

choices.label: Cook their favourite meal
choices.outcome_text: I slightly burnt the edges. They ate every bite and knew exactly what it meant.

choices.label: Leave a silly apology note
choices.outcome_text: The note was terrible. That was the point. We laughed by lunch.

events.title: The Thaw
events.text: After the fight with {person:partner}, neither of us apologised, but they made my coffee this morning. Just the way I like it.

choices.label: Receive it warmly
choices.outcome_text: I drank the apology coffee and said thank you like it meant everything. It did.

choices.label: Bring home a pastry tonight
choices.outcome_text: A pastry on the table said what we were both too stubborn to. We are getting there.

events.title: They Remembered
events.text: {person:lover} remembered our anniversary before I did, and there are candles where the bills usually pile up.

choices.label: Cherish every second
choices.outcome_text: We ate by candlelight and remembered out loud. I fell for them all over again.

choices.label: Reveal the gift I hid
choices.outcome_text: Their face when they unwrapped it — I would pay that thirty-five dollars a hundred times.

events.title: Calendar Blindness
events.text: I forgot our anniversary. {person:lover} is being very understanding in a way that is somehow worse than shouting.

choices.label: Make real amends
choices.outcome_text: I planned a whole make-up evening and swore a silent oath to my calendar.

choices.label: Blame how busy I've been
choices.outcome_text: Busy is a bad apology. They accepted it, which somehow felt worse.

events.title: Another Year Of Us
events.text: Another year with {person:lover}. The tradition is that we do something we have never done before.

choices.label: A day trip somewhere new
choices.outcome_text: We got pleasantly lost, found a tiny bakery, and agreed it was our new tradition.

choices.label: Recreate our first date at home
choices.outcome_text: Same food, same terrible playlist, same butterflies. Cheaper than the original, sweeter too.

choices.label: Watch the stars from the porch
choices.outcome_text: We dragged a blanket onto the porch and counted shooting stars badly. Free and perfect.
